title: Holiday Hours Changed? Check the Delivery Orders You Already Accepted
summary: Changed your restaurant’s holiday hours? Compare accepted pickup and delivery orders with staffed handoff times and resolve conflicts before closing.
body_markdown:
If holiday hours changed after customers placed orders, check every accepted pickup and delivery order against the times your kitchen and handoff team can actually cover.


Keep orders you can serve as promised. For any order that no longer fits, assign a manager to resolve it through the marketplace’s approved process. Changing hours for new orders is not proof that an existing order changed.


## Find orders that overlap the closure


Start with each affected location and marketplace. Check the merchant order view for orders already accepted, including orders scheduled for later. Record the promised pickup or delivery time in store-local time and the expected kitchen and handoff windows. For delivery, distinguish the customer’s delivery time from the time the kitchen needs to hand the order to a courier. Use the timing shown in the actual merchant workflow.


DoorDash documents a separate[Scheduled view in Business Manager](https://merchants.doordash.com/en-us/learning-center/live-order-management) . Uber Eats documents[Holiday Hours in Uber Eats Manager](https://help.uber.com/merchants-and-restaurants/article/updating-your-service-hours-address-and-phone-number?nodeId=5028e125-10aa-4a5f-8bd0-48924d85bec0) that take priority over normal menu hours, including for point-of-sale (POS) integrated stores. These are separate checks: one is about orders on the books, the other about the availability shown to customers.


## Decide which orders you can still fulfill


Say the kitchen will now close at 4:30 p.m. and the pickup counter is staffed until 5 p.m. A prepaid 4:45 p.m. pickup can stay on the books if it can be prepared, held and handed off as promised. A 5:15 p.m. pickup does not fit. A delivery order may have a different outcome if the required courier handoff falls within the staffed window. Confirm the actual times before deciding.


- Can serve as promised:


Confirm capacity and assign the handoff to the closing shift.
- Cannot serve as promised:


Have a named manager check what adjustment or cancellation the platform permits, communicate through the approved channel and record the outcome. Do not quietly move a pickup time or promise a change before it is confirmed.
- Timing unclear:


Check with the team or marketplace and leave the order open on the exception list until it has a decision.


## Close the shift with an exception list


Record the location, marketplace order reference, promised time, owner and outcome. Keep customer contact information in the approved system, not a shared checklist. Before closing, have the manager confirm there are no unresolved orders without an owner, then verify that the public listing no longer offers new order slots beyond the revised hours.


Does changing holiday hours cancel scheduled orders?


Don’t assume it does. Check the status of each accepted order in the applicable merchant tool and follow the platform’s process if the order can’t be fulfilled as placed.


For store-level online and offline visibility across connected delivery marketplaces, explore[Voosh Marketplace Store Uptime](https://www.voosh.ai/marketplace-store-uptime) . Use the marketplace order view for individual orders and exceptions.
